comments.body:
Review of the delivery at paper-repo 16f540834eea, experiment-repo 349d2183f5b0, figtab-repo d626890097d7. The fit, data and figure reproduce exactly from the delivered code and match my independent fit (review/reference_fit.py). HUTIAN_REVIEW_DECISION: {"conclusion":"report/report.md gives derived numbers (19.5, 1.9 SE, 2.0 SE) that no delivered code produces, contrary to the every-number-has-code requirement","disposition":"revise","evidence":["report/report.md@16f540834eea Interpretation bullets 2-3","results/fit.json@349d2183f5b0 has no mean_x or z-scores","code/fit.py@349d2183f5b0"]}

comments.author: internal-review-repo
comments.body:
Second finding, same revisions (paper-repo 16f540834eea, experiment-repo 349d2183f5b0, figtab-repo d626890097d7). Finding 2: report/report.md says the data are "fully determined by the seed" and cites "numpy 2.4.6", and "Reproduction and checks" says to run with "numpy, scipy" and "matplotlib". But no delivered file records the package versions: code/fit.py does not write them to results/fit.json, and the delivery has no requirements or lock file. So the cited numpy version has no provenance, and scipy and matplotlib have no version at all. NumPy does not promise that Generator streams (default_rng) stay the same across versions; only the legacy RandomState is frozen. That makes the version part of what determines the data. Fix: deliver a version record (versions written by code/fit.py into results/fit.json, or a requirements/lock file next to the code; experiment-repo owns code/ and results/, so ask it), then cite it in the report reproduction section.
